raw_text: I am member_002 (independent reviewer). Please publish your fixed candidate for the "nested classmethod as Field.default" deconstruct issue with fix_patch, then send me a handoff_patch so I can integrate, run the same-version public tests, and record an accept/request-changes review. Tip: the fix likely belongs in django/db/migrations/serializer.py (TypeSerializer/DeconstructableSerializer) or django/db/migrations/autodetector.py where EnumType-based defaults are serialized; check django.db.models.fields.Field / django.utils.deconstruct plus django/db/models/enums.py__qualname__ handling. Also tell me which public test module you target (e.g. migrations.test_writer / migrations.test_autodetector).

Candidate patch-1 (source v6) is published for independent review.

Fix location: django/db/migrations/serializer.py, FunctionTypeSerializer, bound-classmethod branch. The bug is exactly the one you pointed at: it used klass.__name__ (only the nested class name, e.g. "Capability"), so Profile.Capability.default serialized as "appname.models.Capability.default". Changed to klass.__qualname__, which yields "appname.models.Profile.Capability.default" as the issue requires. One line:
- return "%s.%s.%s" % (module, klass.__name__, self.value.__name__), {"import %s" % module}
+ return "%s.%s.%s" % (module, klass.__qualname__, self.value.__name__), {"import %s" % module}

Regression test: tests/migrations/test_writer.py adds a nested TextChoices subclass with a classmethod (TestModel1.Capability.get_default) and test_serialize_nested_class_method, asserting the serialized string is "migrations.test_writer.TestModel1.Capability.get_default", the import set, and round-trip equality. Note bound classmethods are re-created per attribute access, so round-trip compares by equality, not identity.

My own same-version evidence on v6: django selection targets ["migrations.test_writer", "migrations.test_autodetector"] => 229 tests, 0 failures/errors, validation_status verified (report test-report-acc38cc1ce0184e2681a19e1).

Please integrate_patch(patch-1), run public tests on that exact adopted version, and record accept or request_changes via org_review_patch. Reply with any failure output if you request changes.

Review complete: review-1 = ACCEPT for patch-1 (source v6, files_sha256 0de9ef2a...).

Evidence I ran myself on my adopted copy (v2 = patch-1 integrated, no conflicts):
- migrations.test_writer: 54/54 passed (incl. your new test_serialize_nested_class_method) — report test-report-22cb190ec7949b2c9b3ab4f3
- migrations.test_autodetector: 175/175 passed — report test-report-5891c14a743043e9b65ece76 (this is the evidence bound to the acceptance)
Note: one intermediate run of mine showed errors=1; that was my own bad label ("migrations.test_serializer" does not exist in this checkout), not a code failure.

Code check: FunctionTypeSerializer's bound-classmethod branch now uses klass.__qualname__, producing "appname.models.Profile.Capability.default" per the issue; consistent with the EnumSerializer branch above it which already uses __qualname__.

You are the delivery member. Please proceed on your side: ensure your current tree is exactly this accepted version, run_tests on it, fix_patch(task_ids=[]), then submit_integration. I have no further edits to request.
